corrections: Dedicated F-15C MSIP model replaces generic twin-fin fighter: per-station nose/body, single canopy, separate ramp intakes and twin engine fairings, exposed exhaust actuator rods and complete inward-facing nozzle lining.

Uniform top overlay exposed forward trailing-edge and leading-edge errors; corrected cropped-delta planform, flap hinge, tail leading edge and wing height. Side/front drawings independently checked against stated dimensions.

MSIP FO-3 panel rather than early F-15A or F-15E panel: upper-left VSD, lower-left MPCD, central HUD/communications controls, central ADI/HSI, separate standby trio, right paired engine instruments and knee panels.

Recessed attitude cards through panel apertures. Corrected panel capture depth, cockpit-liner protrusions and seated forward eye clearance. Replaced generic numeric keypad with control groups based on the MSIP foldout.

TAS, geometric altitude including signed readout, climb, true heading, attitude, AoA in degrees, load factor and standby instruments use shared expressions. Unsupported engine/navigation/radar quantities show dashes/INOP; missing readings and gear lamps hide.
Animated ailerons, differential stabilators, rudders, flaps, gear, central stick, pedals and paired left throttles. Exported geometry tests check directions and cardinal heading readings.
Selected geometric seams, canopy fasteners, wing fastener rows and warning stencils. Seat, harness, console groups and footwell modeled without photo textures or external weapons.
independentDimensions: SAC63.75ft length19.431m,42.81ft wingspan13.048488m,18.58ft fin height5.663184m,12ft canopy height3.6576m; runtime fin-mounted fairing extends height to5.71m.
Main axle datum;17.78ft wheelbase5.419344m,9.03ft track2.752344m,28.25ft tail span8.6106m. Wing area56.48504832m2 is specified flight-model area, not a claim of exact triangulated planform area.

Uniform exterior scales use stated length for side and span for top/front. Printed top longitudinal proportions disagree by roughly3–4%; side canopy height and wheelbase also disagree with annotated dimensions. Kept real dimensions and disclosed contour mismatch without stretching reference axes.
MSIP panel scale from nominal3.125in instrument; panel width/depth and seat installation reconstructed from foldout and oblique photographs, not dimensioned manufacturing drawings.
reviewNotes.visual: Inspected four exterior/panel overlays and all eight standard captures. Ten instrument/detail states inspected, with final-hash22captures rechecked in six contact sheets. Full-size canopy/footwell and exhaust close-ups used to correct shell intrusion and inward-surface culling. Compared MSIP foldout plus two cockpit/canopy photos and an independent USAF exterior photograph.
limitations: Polygonal F-15C interpretation combining1989 MSIP cockpit with1992 F100-PW-220 SAC. Printed diagram inconsistencies leave visible canopy, aft-tail and wing-height differences in overlays. Exact airfoil, curvature and small fairings are approximated.

Instrument positions follow the foldout, while dial calibration, bezels, switch counts, console spacing, seat/harness, gear mechanisms and individual fastener placement remain simplified. No complete rivet, stencil, serial-number or unit-livery reproduction.

TAS replaces indicated airspeed; altitude is geometric, heading true, AoA degrees. No calibrated pitot/static IAS/Mach, pressure altitude, magnetic variation, flight-director/nav steering or real engine/fuel systems.

VSD,MPCD and TEWS are inactive; HUD is physical glass without collimated symbology. Engine core RPM,EGT,nozzle schedule,fuel/oil/hydraulic data and clock are unsupported and blank. Static console switches do not implement aircraft systems.
Shared simplified flight dynamics, visual control mixes and gear retraction. Flight smoke proves basic controllability rather than actual F-15 performance; no external stores or weapons behavior.
Reference PDFs and photos retained only as local study evidence. Sources and licenses cited; no reference pixels redistributed as model textures.

instrumentReview.checks: 15 shared imported instrument tests and targeted F-15C geometry test passed, including cardinal heading, control directions, negative altitude and missing-data lamps.

limitations: The SAC sheet is not one scale. Its side overlay understates heights by about 8 percent and its plan view is about 2 percent long, so tail stations read short there. Neither is corrected by stretching a reference.
The drooped cowl is one fixed pose. The real ramps move with angle of attack, so the model is a little low in the inlet face in cruise.
Camouflage is not modeled: the airframe is two flat grays, and the darker wing is a material choice rather than the Mod Eagle pattern.
The apex of the cowl is the least certain landmark. Two photographs place it 5.7 to 6.8 m ahead of the main axle, depending on the view, and the drawing value was kept.

calibration.sheet: SAC page 2, native 3507 by 2551 px. The sheet is not one scale: 46.98 px/m along the body from the 63.75 ft bar, 51.1 px/m up from the static ground line from the 12.00 ft canopy bar, 44.2 px/m across the plan from the 42.81 ft bar and 43.75 px/m on the front view. Its drawn wheelbase is 5.15 m against the annotated 5.42 m.
calibration.resolution: Annotated dimensions win. The 12.00 ft crown was confirmed by the matched photograph, 3.65 m at 108 px/m, so the drawn vertical scale is the error rather than the annotation.
calibration.photoChecks: Back-projected onto the centerline plane, held-out heights agree with the station tables to about 0.08 m once the 7 px bias at the nose wheel is removed.

proportionPass.finding: The owner reported a wrong nose and an oversized cockpit. The canopy length and width were close. The fault was a forebody too slim and shallow to carry it, so the same canopy looked oversized.

measured.landmark: Forebody depth, keel to rail at the seat (m)
Cowl rake, apex to lower lip (m)
Body half-breadth at the inlet lip / wing trailing edge (m)

corrections: Forebody, canopy and dorsal spine rebuilt from traced station tables. The canopy is long and low, tapers into a real spine hump, and sits on a rail that rises toward the seat.
Airframe moved 0.22 m forward of the gear. The solved photograph and the drawn nose gear both put the nose about 6.4 m ahead of it. The annotated wheelbase is kept.
Inlets narrowed and raked. The cowl rests drooped about 8 degrees, as both photographs show on the ground; the SAC draws it level. This is a static choice, not an animated ramp.

Plan flare added from the inlet lip to the wing root, and wing moved 0.46 m forward. Close-set round engines, tail booms, the notch between the nozzles, the stabilator dogtooth and a rudder confined to the lower half of the fin replace the straight box and center spike.
Cockpit tub liner raised to the higher rail, bulkhead added behind the seat, anti-glare deck added under the windscreen, HUD lowered clear of the crown. Panel positions and instruments are unchanged.

Radome reshaped after the owner reported it needle-like. Depth already matched the photograph, but traced noise had left a concave pinch behind a sharp tip. Stations now follow the photograph with a convex crown and a rounded tip, and the radome is closer to the body color so it does not read as a dark spike.

cockpitSweep.finding: The seat stood 0.78 m behind the eye, and the HUD control box filled the view over the nose.
changes: Eye raised 3.34 to 3.42 m, inside the canopy crown of about 3.64 m.
Instrument panel lowered 0.08 m as a unit; the clear combiner keeps its height and now runs down to the mount.
Seat forward 0.46 m and up 0.29 m; stick forward 0.21 m and 0.29 m taller; pedals aft 0.26 m and up 0.08 m; throttles forward 0.34 m; consoles up 0.12 m.
Bulkhead behind the seat and an avionics deck close the bay the seat left. Exterior geometry unchanged.
limitations: Seat, stick, pedal and throttle positions come from seated-eye ergonomic targets and cockpit photographs, not a dimensioned installation drawing.
The deck behind the seat is a plain reconstruction, not a traced layout.
